logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of the synthesized compounds was evaluated using the classical shake-flask method reported in the literature. For this purpose, the synthesized ligands and half-sandwich Ru(II) complexes were used to determine the octanol/water partition coefficient (LogP) in a system consisting of saturated potassium phosphate buffer and 1-octanol. The compounds were first dissolved in saturated potassium phosphate (PBS) buffer and subsequently mixed with an equal volume of saturated 1-octanol. The mixture was shaken at room temperature for 30 min to allow equilibrium between the two phases. Afterward, the samples were centrifuged for 15 min and allowed to stand until complete phase separation occurred. The distribution of the compounds between the aqueous and organic phases was quantified by UV-Vis spectroscopic analysis at their respective absorption wavelengths. The measured concentrations were then applied to the appropriate equation to calculate the Log P (partition coefficient) values.
